Rules 1, 9, 11, 16, 17. | 20 Nov checker: "Some labels are being overlapped": I moved only tick labels so none touch each other or the circle: x labels -6, -5, -4 nudged left and -2 and 1 nudged slightly so -5/-4 and -3/-2 no longer run together and 1 clears the circle, and y labels -1, -4 and -5 nudged down, up and down so -1 clears the x label 1 and -4 and -5 clear the circle.

y = 1 - cos x and y = sin x on 0..pi, 0.9pt, at the crop's scale. The end dot at (pi,2) is kept. The shaded region (under 1 - cos x up to pi/2, then under sin x) uses house shade hatch reverse, matching the crop's back-slash hatching. The tick marks cross the axes as in the crop. pi/2 is written as \dfrac (rule 23), so it is a little taller than the crop's small fraction. The remaining colour in the overlay is hatch-line phase. Rules 1, 5, 5a, 9, 23, 27.

Solution sketch of y = x(x-2)(x+1), drawn from the true cubic (rules 10, 16). Dots at the intercepts -1, 0, 2, the max (-0.55,0.63), the min (1.22,-2.11) and the POI (1/3,-20/27), with labels as in the solution; the POI label uses \dfrac. Left out: the green marking notes and the colours (rules 6, 17). The axes are straightened (the crop's y-axis is tilted). Approx because the hand sketch is not to any scale: its tails are flatter and its max/min ratio differs, so the true curve cannot match it exactly. The scale is chosen to fit the roots, so the overlay is low by nature. No x/y axis labels, as in the crop.

Solution sketch of y = tan(x/2) on (-pi, pi): true curve at 0.9pt with arrows, dashed asymptotes at x = ±pi, dots at (±pi/2, ±1). Ticks are evenly spaced at pi/4 steps and integers ±1..±4, with fraction labels as \dfrac. Left out: the question text cut into the top of the crop, and the scan wobble (rules 10, 17). The -pi/2 dot is at its true y = -1, where the sketch drew it near -1.4 (rule 16). The -pi/4 and -pi/2 labels sit below the curve, because the space just under the axis is the curve region (rules 11, 24). Please check -3pi/4: the curve passes close to that label, and it sits tight beside the -pi label. The overlay is low because of the hand-drawn strokes and the dropped header text. | 21 Nov checker: "Try to keep all the xaxis labels on hte same line" (owner: "you decide for the diagram to be usable"): One shared line is impossible because the curve runs below the axis on the left and above it on the right, so the x labels stay below the axis on one baseline and only -pi/2 and -pi/4, which would sit on the curve and the (-pi/2, -1) dot, moved just above the axis centred on their ticks (-3pi/4 keeps a 9 px gap to the curve at 200 dpi, so it stays below); -pi now sits just left of the left dashed asymptote on the same baseline, mirroring pi on the right, with the x-axis extended slightly left, so it no longer reads as one expression with -3pi/4.

y = ln(x^2) drawn true (2 ln x) through the crop's P(1,0) and Q(e,2) positions. R is plotted at its true point (e-1, ln(e-1)^2) (rule 16), so it sits further right than in the crop: the crop's curve is not a true ln curve between P and Q. Triangle PQR is outlined, with a dashed guide from Q down to e. Shading: the crop has very dense fine vertical lines, drawn here with the house shade hatch, which is sparser in the thin sliver; the owner may prefer flat grey 'shade'. The overlay difference is mainly the crop's more strongly bent curve and R's position. Rules 1, 5, 9, 10, 12, 16.

Two-way survey table, so it is transcribed, not drawn (rule 8). Title 'Survey results' is the caption. Header wraps where the paper wraps; the corner cell and the totals-row label are empty as on the paper. Words are in \text{} (12 Nov ruling).

table.caption: Survey results

notes: Venn diagram: rectangle and two equal intersecting circles measured from the crop pixels. Region values 8, 7, 11 and 3 are placed as in the crop. Round 2 moved the box's bottom edge down to match. A and B are maths italic instead of the scan's bold upright (rule 19). Lines are 0.6pt black (rule 3) and labels sit clear of every line (rule 11).

Venn diagram: rectangle and two intersecting circles measured from the crop pixels. Region labels x, 2, 5 and 5 are placed as in the crop. Round 2 fixed the box's right and bottom edges. A and B are maths italic instead of the scan's bold upright (rule 19). Lines are 0.6pt black (rule 3) and labels sit clear of every line (rule 11).

Cubic fitted through the crop's roots b, 0, a; turning points match the crop. Region between the curve and the x-axis from b to a shaded flat grey. Both axes have arrows at both ends, as in the crop. Curve 0.9pt (rule 9). Round 1 failed to compile (dimension too large); I rescaled the variable to fix it. Rules 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11.

Clean redraw of the solution sketch of y=6x^2-x^3 on a true scale (48 px per x unit, 6.4 px per y unit). Ticks 2, 4, 6 and 32, 16 are evenly spaced. Max (4,32) and inflexion (2,16) sit at their computed positions, with dashed guides and a dot at the inflexion. I dropped the teacher's stray tick on the y-axis and the uneven tick spacing. The left branch is steeper and narrower than the hand sketch because the true curve is used (sketch was not to scale). That accounts for most of the red/blue. Rules 10, 16, 17, 4, 9, 12.

y=|x-2| drawn on a true 59 px/unit scale with verticals at x=-1 and x=4. The two triangles under the graph are hatched with house shade hatch; the crop's hand hatch strokes are replaced. Dashed guides at heights 3 and 2, and dots at (0,2) and (2,0). I dropped the teacher's stray marks on the x-axis and the scan border line at the right edge, which shifts the overlay alignment. The rest of the low score is hand-stroke wobble and hatch placement. Rules 5, 10, 16, 17, 12. | 20 Nov checker: "Make the dotted line go to touch the y-axis": The dashed guide at height 2 now starts at the y-axis (the dot at (0,2)) instead of stopping short at x = 1.05, so it touches the y-axis.

Both parabolas on the crop's true scale (67.5 px per x unit, 32 px per y unit). The intersections at x=-1 and x=2 match the crop exactly. Curves 0.9pt with filled latex heads at all four ends; the crop's open axis chevrons become latex heads. Equation labels are in the same places. The low score comes from the crop's very heavy curve strokes and large arrowheads (scan stroke thickness), not from geometry. The labels are a little larger than the crop's small labels. Rules 3, 4, 9, 16.

Cylinder with the back half of the base ellipse dashed (aux), a centre dot with radius r, and the h dimension arrow broken around its label with end bars. Labels at normal size. Rules 2, 3, 4, 11. | 20 Nov checker: "The r label is touching the cylinder lines. Fix": The r label is moved slightly left and down to the middle of the gap between the back rim and the radius line, and set one size smaller (small), so it now clears both lines by a visible 2-3 px gap at 200 dpi. | 21 Nov checker: "move the r label into the center of the radius lineandon top making sure that it doesnt touch the otherlines": The r label is now centred over the midpoint of the radius line, just above it, with a 2 px clear gap to both the radius line and the back rim at 200 dpi; normal size (12pt) does not fit in that gap, so r is set at 9pt, the largest size that keeps that gap (one step smaller than the 20 Nov small size).

I drew y=-4+3sin2x from its equation at 0.9pt over 0<=x<=2pi, with pi at about 292 px, so it matches the crop's peaks, troughs and 2pi end. Axes are drawn level (the scan tilts). There are dashed guides at -1 and -7 to the first maximum and minimum, and dashed verticals at pi and 2pi. Ticks at -4 and -7, labels -1, -4, -7, pi, 2pi, x and y in maths font. The score is low because of hand-wobble in the teacher's curve (troughs below -7), the thick scan strokes and the handwritten labels. I checked the layout by eye. Rules 1, 3, 4, 9, 10, 11, 17.

Increasing concave-down curve from O, drawn as y=A(1-e^{-0.75x}) and fitted to the crop's point at x=1 and its end point. It has an end arrow and a dot on the curve at x=1, with a tick and label 1. The crop's open arrow chevron is replaced by the house filled Latex head. Rules 1, 3a, 4, 9, 16.

Both branches of y=3+1/(x+2) are drawn from the equation (0.9pt, arrows where the crop has them). I used one x scale (81 px/unit) and one y scale (65 px/unit) chosen to split the error between the crop's asymptote and intercept positions. The teacher's sketch is not to scale: intercepts sit about 13 px from the crop and the asymptotes about 10-13 px. The crossings at 7/2 and -7/3 are the true crossings of the drawn curve. Fractions are stacked. Left out: the teacher's working in the top right and the stray '2'. Blue becomes black dashed. The score is low mainly from the dropped working text, the handwriting and the teacher's curve hugging the asymptotes less closely than the true function. Rules 1, 6, 9, 16, 17, 23.

The curve is smooth Bezier pieces through (-6,0), (-4,5), (0,0), (2,-2), (4,0), flat at both turning points, on one uniform scale (32 px/unit in x, 17.5 px/unit in y). Each turning point therefore sits at its true coordinate: the crop draws the max about 15 px right of where uniform scaling puts it. There are arrows at both ends, filled house heads instead of the crop's open axis chevrons and bold heads. Labels are in maths font with a proper minus sign. The remaining colour is label glyph differences and the crop's heavy arrowheads. Rules 1, 4, 9, 16.

Smooth Bezier curve through (-10,0), (-6,5), (2,0), (6,-2), (10,0), flat at both turning points, with a dot and label at each. Ticks and labels at -10, 2 and 10. I moved the y-axis about 20 px right so the intercepts and turning points sit at true coordinates on one uniform scale: the teacher's sketch puts the axis at about x=-1. The y-axis is redrawn with its arrow at the top and a y label. The teacher's downward arrowhead at the bottom was dropped, but the long axis length is kept. The score is low from handwriting, the scan strokes and the moved axis. Rules 1, 4, 9, 16, 17. | 20 Nov checker: "Make the curve smoother and make it the actual graph": The hand-placed Bezier curve is replaced by a TikZ plot (100 samples, smooth) of a degree-7 polynomial through the true x-intercepts -10, 2, 10 and the turning points (-6,5) and (6,-2) with zero slope there and no other turning points, so the curve is the true transformed graph at the same scale, with axes, ticks, labels, dots and end arrows unchanged.

Redrew y=e^x-1 on a light grey unit grid from x=-4 to 4 and y=-3 to 2, using the crop's scale and positions (1 unit = 73 px). The curve is plotted from its equation at 0.9pt, smooth with 90 samples, from x=-4 up to y of about 2.4, with an arrowhead (rules 9, 10, 3a). The y=-1 asymptote is drawn with the house aux dashes and a left arrowhead, as in the crop. Both axes have double-headed filled Latex arrows, as in the crop. Changes from the crop: (1) the red teacher scribble along the bottom and the hand-drawn chevrons are removed (rules 4, 17); (2) everything is black and grey (rule 6); (3) I added a 'y=-1' label below the asymptote because the solution says the asymptote is labelled (rule 18); (4) the 0 label is moved to the lower right of the origin and the -1 label to just below the dashed line, so neither touches the curve or the asymptote (rule 11). Tick labels are a little larger than the crop's tiny scan text so they can be read. The overlay is below 0.85 only because of the removed scribble, the hand-drawn arrowheads and axis letters, label font differences and the y-axis being about 1 px off.
Axes with y, O, x labels; arc drawn as a half-ellipse at 0.9pt (rule 9) with the crop's endpoints (x=162,458 px) and top height. Filled latex arrowheads (rule 4). Rules 1,2,3,4,9 applied.

Normal curve drawn from the Gaussian formula (rule 10) at the crop's peak position and height, 0.9pt; flat grey shading between the 25 and 145 ticks down to the double-arrowed axis (rule 5); dashed mean line in house aux style. Round 1 did not compile (pgfmath overflow). The low overlay score comes from the original's tails, which are heavier than a true normal's: the redraw's tails sit lower, and the scan's heavy grey fill is lighter in the redraw. Both are deliberate under rules 10 and 5. Peak, shoulders, ticks and labels line up.

Solution sketch: circle with centre C(-2,-3) tangent to the x-axis, dashed radius from the tangent point to the centre dot, labelled sqrt d. The C(-2,-3) label is moved slightly left so it ends before the y-axis, which it crosses in the crop (rule 11). Remaining colour is scan stroke thickness and small glyph offsets. | 20 Nov checker: "Move the C label more to the right slightly as it is touching the circle": The C(-2,-3) label is moved 4 px right so it clears the circle while still ending before the y-axis.

Box plot at 0.9pt (rule 9) at the crop's positions; cumulative frequency curve at 0.9pt from O, a smooth spline through measured points (steep start, flat middle, steep finish). Italic captions centred under each plot. The curve is a hand-fitted spline; desmooth.py was not available. Remaining colour: the curve's middle section is a few px off, plus stroke thickness from 0.9pt over the crop's thin lines.
Option A: 7 equal bars, all the same height, on arrowed axes. Bars at 0.9pt (rule 9: graph touching the axis) and the same style as the other options (rule 7).
Option B: symmetric peaked histogram, 7 bars. Pairs of bar heights made exactly symmetric (tiny scan differences dropped, rule 10). Bars at 0.9pt, same frame as the other options (rule 7).
Option C: symmetric U-shaped histogram, 7 bars. Heights made symmetric (rule 10). Bars at 0.9pt, same frame as the other options (rule 7).
Histogram for option D: 7 bars on the same edges and heights as the crop, bars drawn at 0.9pt, axes 0.6pt with filled latex heads (rules 1, 3, 4, 9). No labels in the crop.
Straight cumulative-frequency line from O, drawn at 0.9pt; axes with filled latex heads. The O label (half cut off in the crop) is drawn whole, left of the origin (rules 1, 4, 9, 11).

S-shaped cumulative-frequency curve fitted to the crop as one smooth spline at 0.9pt. This used 3 rounds: round 2 made the fit worse, so round 3 refitted the curve to the overlay. O label drawn whole (rules 1, 3a, 9).

Two graphs side by side. f is drawn as a symmetric cubic (y = kx^3, flat at O). g is an exponential with the house dashed asymptote on the x-axis. Open chevrons replaced by filled latex heads; labels at \small to match the paper's size. Round 1 did not compile (pgf number overflow), so there were 2 real drawing rounds. Remaining red/blue is the scan's heavy dashes (the house aux dash is finer) and a small difference in text width (rules 2, 3, 4, 10).

Option A: quartic-like U shape fitted to the crop's vertex, intercepts and end heights, drawn symmetric about the y-axis. The crop's right branch is slightly narrower, which is pen unevenness (rule 10). Round 1 did not compile, so there were 2 real drawing rounds. Filled arrowheads; labels at \small (rules 1, 4, 10).

Option B: Gaussian bump with arrowheads on both ends along the asymptote. The x-axis is drawn as the house fine dashed asymptote with a solid arrow tip, as on the paper. The label 'asymptote at y = 0' is at \small. Remaining red is the scan's heavy dashes (rules 3, 4, 10, 12).
Option C: horizontal rays joined by a smooth sine step through O, with filled latex arrowheads on the ray ends; labels at \small (rules 4, 10, 12).

Option D: decaying exponential y=27e^{-0.0527(x-248)} in crop pixels, fitted to the crop's y-intercept and left-hand top end, with arrows at both ends, 0.9pt because it runs along the axis (rule 9). The asymptote is drawn in house aux dashes along the x-axis (rule 3), with the label 'asymptote at y = 0'. The remaining red/blue is the hand-sketched curve, which decays more slowly than a true exponential just right of the y-axis. Rule 10 says to draw it from the maths, so the curve was not traced. Rules 1, 3, 4, 9, 10 and 11 applied.

Piecewise graph: y=1 on [-2,0], joined to y=1-x^2 (exact, rule 10/16), drawn down to x=2.24 with an arrow. Ticks at ±2 and ±4 on both axes. Curve 0.9pt (rule 9). It crosses the x-axis at x=1, slightly left of where the sketch crosses (rule 16). In round 2 the axis lengths and tick-label positions were moved to match the crop. Rules 1, 4, 9, 10, 12, 16 and 24 applied.

Drawn with the house tree template (rule 21), so the low overlay score is expected. Level-1 labels are stacked like the paper ('prohibited / items', 'no / prohibited / items'). 5/100 and 95/100 are on the first branches. The four answer boxes (40x30pt) sit in the probability slots: above the up branches, below the down branches. Level-1 spacing is wider than the crop so the boxes of the two middle branches do not crowd each other. Round 1 had a column-width bug (labels sat on the branches); fixed by measuring the label widths outside the picture. Rules 14, 21 and 23 applied.

Completed tree in the house tree template (rule 21); the overlay is low because the layout is standardised, not traced. Second-stage probabilities 95/100, 5/100, 2/100 and 98/100 are bold as on the paper (the answers), stacked fractions (rule 23), above the up branches and below the down branches. Round 1 failed to compile (\bf macro name clash); fixed in round 2. Rules 14, 21 and 23 applied.

Scatterplot: the 28 dots visible in the crop, placed at their measured positions. Regression line 0.9pt, passing through the marked point (180,184), with aux dashed guides to both axes that meet at that point (rule 12). Axis titles as on the paper, the y title rotated. Round 2 set the dot size and 11pt labels to match the crop. Rules 1, 2, 3, 9 and 12 applied.

y=sqrt(x)(1-x) on [0,1] drawn exactly (parametrised by sqrt(x) so it is smooth at the origin), 0.9pt. The region under it is flat grey (house shade, a lighter tone than the scan, rule 5). Tick at 1; the equation label is clear of the curve. Rules 1, 3a, 5, 9, 10 and 27 applied.

Basketball diagram. The dashed path is the solved parabola y=-23/630 x^2+367/630 x+2, mapped onto the crop's not-to-scale layout. It passes through the ball, the top of the 4 m arrow and the rim, and ends in a filled arrowhead (rules 4, 10, 12). Dimension arrows (2 m, 5 m, 4 m, 3 m, 14 m) have their labels in gaps in the lines like the paper (rule 11). The hoop, net, backboard and grey pole are simplified line art; the ball is grey with seams; 'NOT TO SCALE' is kept. The ground line is 0.6pt instead of the scan's heavier stroke (rule 3). The 4 m arrow is about 4 px right of the crop's so it meets the drawn path. Rules 1, 3, 4, 6, 10, 11 and 12 applied.

Basketball solution sketch on cartesian axes, drawn in crop pixel units. Axes have filled latex arrows; dashed guides (house aux) at heights 4 and 3 drop to x = 5 and x = 14; grey ball at (0,2); hoop, backboard and pole are light grey; NOT TO SCALE text kept. The trajectory is a true parabola fitted through the three marked crop positions (0,2), (5,4), (14,3) and drawn at 0.9pt (rules 10, 16). Its peak sits about 15 px higher than the scan's hand-drawn arc, and that accounts for most of the red/blue (score below 0.85). Net drawn as simple clean strokes. Rules 1, 3, 4, 9, 10, 12, 16.

Excavation site: 150 x 60 rectangle with a centre line. The irregular region is traced from the crop as one smooth spline (plot smooth, not every pixel) with flat light-grey shading, as in the crop (rule 5). Offset lines at the three verticals are solid inside the region and dashed (aux) outside it. Labels 25, 17, 33, 26, 18, 18 m sit right of their lines; the 60 m and 150 m dimension arrows use filled latex heads instead of the crop's open chevrons (rule 4). Scores are just under 0.85 because of small label offsets and the scan's stroke thickness. Rules 1, 3, 4, 5, 6a.

3D bearing diagram: P, Q, R, X at crop positions; NW and NE arrows with filled latex heads; right-angle marks at X; 10 degree arc at P and 5 degree arc at Q are true circular arcs centred on the vertex and ending on both arms (rules 14, 22); 100 m double-arrow dimension parallel to PQ with a rotated label (rule 6a); NW/NE in bold as in the crop; NOT TO SCALE kept. Remaining colour is small label offsets only. Rules 1, 3, 4, 11, 14, 22. | 20 Nov checker: "Fix the right angle markers especially the one on the left. Move the 5 degree slightly highter. samewith teh10degree angle": Both right-angle marks at X are enlarged to match the paper (24 px between XR and XQ, 18 px between XR and XP, each a parallelogram along its two arms), the 5 degree label is moved 8 px up and the 10 degree label about 38 px up so it sits clear of both arms above its arc.
Blank h–t axes at the crop's size and origin position, filled latex arrowheads, italic h and t labels. Rules 2, 4, 19.

h = 5 + 3 sin(pi t/4) on [0,24], drawn from the equation at the crop's scale (20.7 px per hour, evenly spaced ticks 2, 5, 8) at 0.9pt with 90 smooth samples (rules 3a, 9, 10). Dashed h = 5 line and dashed drops at t = 8, 16, 24; end point dot at (24,5); tick labels on the same sides as the crop. Round 2 moved the axes and lowered the score (round 1 was 0.823/0.743): the x-axis is now a few px off the scan and the y-axis arrow runs a little longer. The rest of the colour is the 0.9pt curve against the scan's thin stroke. Shape and labels match. Check the axis position first. Rules 1, 3, 4, 9, 10, 24.

Curve drawn from f(x) = x/(1+x^2), which has exactly the stated features: through O, max (1, 1/2), min (-1, -1/2), x-axis asymptote. Scaled to the crop (47 px per x unit, 86 px per y unit); it lies over the scan's curve, tails included. Drawn at 0.9pt (rules 9, 10). Turning-point dots are at the computed points (rule 16), with \dfrac labels in large brackets (rule 23). The asymptote is drawn as the crop shows it: the x-axis itself dashed (aux) with a solid arrowhead. Rules 1, 4, 9, 10, 11, 16, 23.
Blank x–y axes with origin O, at the crop's size and position, filled latex arrowheads. Rules 2, 4, 19.

Drew y = 1 - 6x/(9+x^2), which is -2f(x/3)+1 with f(x)=x/(1+x^2), the f that fits the given features. Curve 0.9pt with arrows at both ends, house fine dashes for the asymptote y=1, and dots at (-3,2), (0,1), (3,0) placed at their computed positions. The original sketch is not to a consistent scale: its max sits at 2.27 units above the axis while y=1 sits 59 px up. I used a compromise y-scale of 63 px/unit, so the maximum and the left tail sit about 8 px lower and the asymptote about 4 px higher than in the crop. Most of the low overlay score comes from that and from the dash pattern. Rules 1, 3, 3a, 4, 9, 10, 16.
Blank x-y axes at the crop's position, with filled latex arrowheads and labels x, y, O. Rules 2, 3, 4, 19.

Drew y=2x e^{-x} from its equation at 34 px/unit across and 50 px/unit up, from x=-0.9 to 6.5. Curve 0.9pt with filled arrows at both ends. The max (1,2/e) and inflection (2,4/e^2) dots are at their true positions. The sketch's points are not to one scale (inflection too far right and too low), so my inflection dot sits about 8 px left of and slightly above the crop's. The labels with stacked fractions sit clear of the curve. The open chevron arrow became a filled latex head. Rules 1, 4, 9, 10, 11, 16, 23.
Blank x-t axes; the vertical axis runs below O to match the crop. Filled arrowheads; labels x, t, O. Rules 2, 3, 4.

Drew x=1-3/(t+1) for t from 0 to 10.8, 0.9pt with an arrow at the end. Dashed asymptote x=1 and ticks at 1, -1 and -2; the t-intercept 2 lies on the true curve. The y-intercept label is written -2: the scan lost the minus sign, and the solution gives x=-2 (rule 18). The vertical axis has arrows at both ends, as in the crop. Rules 4, 9, 10, 16, 18, 24.
An exact equilateral triangle and 5 nested midpoint triangles, built by computing the midpoints, at the crop's size. Lines 0.6pt. Rules 1, 3.

Three concentric circles at the crop's radii, with the outer ring and centre disc shaded in the house flat grey (shade). The crop's grey is a little darker; I made it lighter as rule 5 allows. Three radii with labels 5 cm, 2 cm and 20 cm, plus NOT TO SCALE as two centred lines. Rules 1, 2, 5, 6, 11. Check that the 2 cm label clears the end of its radius.

Corridor corner diagram drawn in crop pixel units: walls, whiteboard L (0.9pt emphasis to match the crop's heavier stroke), passing exactly through the inner corner (rule 12); theta arc centred on the corner; 4 m and 3 m dimension arrows; dashed classroom/entrance arrows with house aux dashes and filled Latex heads (rule 4, replacing the crop's open chevrons). Remaining overlay colour is font-glyph and arrowhead differences. Rules 1,2,3,4,11,12.

Solution sketch with L1/L2 labels, two theta arcs (at the corner and at the wall with a dashed horizontal reference), 4 m and 3 m dimension arrows. Round 2 moved L2 left of the line, enlarged both arcs to the crop's radius and lowered the 3 m arrow to match. Whiteboard drawn as a single straight line through the corner. Rules 1,4,11,12,14,22.

Steep whiteboard position: solid part above, dashed continuation to the outer wall, all on one straight line through the corner (rule 12); theta arc enlarged in round 2; 4 m and 3 m dimension arrows with filled heads. Rules 1,3,4,11,12.
Shallow whiteboard position: solid part then dashed continuation to the top wall, on one line through the corner; large theta arc; 3 m dimension arrow with filled heads. Rules 1,3,4,12.

Several whiteboard positions: one solid (0.9pt) and three dashed (house aux) lines, all passing exactly through the inner corner. In round 2 the horizontal walls were extended to the crop's width. Rules 1,3,12.

New sketch: y=1 from (-2,1) to (0,1), then y=1-x^2 for x>=0 down through (1,0), with an arrow showing it continues downward, all at 0.9pt (rule 9). Closed dot at (-2,1) and dot at (1,0), with labels clear of the curve. A dot at the join point (0,1) could be added if wanted (rule 16). Rules 9,10,12,13,16.

New sketch: ball path y=-23/630 x^2+367/630 x+2 from the player at x=0 until it meets the ground (x about 18.9), plotted from the solution's equation at 0.9pt. Dots and labels at the true points (0,2), (5,4) and (14,3); axes run past the curve. Rules 9,10,13,16.

y = sin x drawn from the equation at the crop's scale (pi/6 = 92 px, 1 = 182 px), 0.9pt with an arrow at the end. Two rectangles with heights sin(pi/6) and sin(pi/3), shaded with shade hatch reverse to match the crop's '\\' lines. Dashed outlines in aux; the shared side at pi/3 is solid as in the crop. Fraction tick labels use \dfrac at \scriptsize. The low redraw score comes from where the hatch lines fall and from the scan's grey strokes; the geometry overlays closely. Rules 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 10, 23.

Circle, dashed radii to the chord ends, solid chord and minor segment shaded with shade hatch reverse. All placed from the crop pixels. The angle at O keeps the crop's drawn opening (about 60 degrees, NOT TO SCALE) and is labelled pi/6 with a true arc of radius 49. The pi/6 label was moved slightly lower so it clears the arc. The low scores come from hatch line placement and the scan's thin grey strokes. Rules 1, 3, 5, 11, 22, 23.

Handwritten solution on grid paper redrawn as a clean exam sketch. Grid paper, colours and hand wobble removed (rules 6, 10, 17). The curve y = 3/(2x+4) - 1 is computed (1 unit = 118 px across, 115 px up), so the vertical asymptote x = -2 and y = -1 sit where the crop has them. The intercepts are dots at their computed points (-1/2, 0) and (0, -1/4) with \dfrac labels (rule 16). Both branches have arrows at both ends; asymptotes are drawn in aux dashes. Branch ends follow the true curve, not the teacher's sketch, so the left branch sits further left than drawn. x and y axis labels added. APPROX: round 2 changed the minor grid to 10 cells per major (0.05 s, 0.5 m), but the paper looks like 5 per major (0.1 s, 1 m). With no rounds left this is not fixed: change the minor grid steps to xstep=0.1, ystep=1. The low redraw score comes from these extra grid lines. Rules 2, 3, 9, 10, 3a, 5b.

Grid with Provider B's line from (0,0) to (1000,350) at 0.9pt. Axes, tick marks, tick labels, rotated y title and x title match the crop. Major grid lines every 100 kWh and $40. APPROX: the minor grid is drawn at 10 cells per major (10 kWh, $5), but the paper appears to have 5 per major (20 kWh, $8). With no rounds left this is not fixed: use xstep=0.2, ystep=8. The low redraw score comes from the extra grid lines. Rules 2, 3, 9, 6.

Solution grid with B: C=0.35x from 0 to 1000 and A: C=40+0.25x from 0 to 1000 (ends at 290), both at 0.9pt. Dots at the computed intersection (400,140) and at the end point (1000,290) (rule 16). APPROX: same minor-grid issue as q21_1. The grid is drawn at 10 cells per major, but the paper appears to have 5 (use xstep=0.2, ystep=8). The low redraw score comes from the extra grid lines. Rules 9, 12, 16.

Wall cross-section copied from the crop (NOT TO SCALE): uprights 1.9/2.7/1.7 m and two curved lower edges meeting in a cusp under the middle upright, fitted as Bezier curves. Also drawn: three right-angle marks, double equal-length ticks on both halves of the top, and a dashed 8.0 m dimension line with filled arrowheads and end bars. Labels and the NOT TO SCALE note are in the crop's positions. The remaining colour is slight curve fit and text-glyph offsets. Rules 1, 3, 4, 11.

Rectangle 8 m by 3 m with the U-shaped 0.5 m path shaded with the house stipple (lighter colour and wider gap, to match the crop's sparse dots), and the garden left unshaded. Also drawn: house walls going up, paired 0.5 m arrows at the top and the right side, a dashed 3 m dimension with end bars, a dashed 8 m dimension with the label in a gap, and a Path leader arrow. Geometry lines match; the low scores come from stipple-dot placement and text offsets. Rules 5, 5a, 4, 3. Checker 23 Nov fix: white box behind each 0.5 m label.

Bearings diagram copied from the crop (NOT TO SCALE): N and E axes through X with bold N/E labels and filled arrowheads, and triangle C-X-Y with XP due south and a right-angle mark at P. The 120 degree bearing arc is a true circle centred on X: it starts on the north line and its arrowhead ends exactly on XY. Labels 40 km, 15 km, NOT TO SCALE are in the crop's positions. Rules 1, 4, 12, 14, 22.

Same bearings diagram as the question, plus the solution's theta (angle CXP) and 60 degree (angle PXY) labels beside XP, as in the solution crop. The 120 degree arc is centred on X and ends on XY. Labels are clear of all lines. The remaining colour is small label and glyph offsets and the NOT TO SCALE position. Rules 1, 11, 12, 18, 22.

This is a typeset table, so I transcribed it instead of drawing it (rule 8, rule 15 spans). The frame line 'Principal and Interest per $1000 borrowed' is kept as the caption subtitle. 'Interest rate (per annum)' spans both header rows. 'Term of loan (years)' spans all six term columns.

notes: Activity network: 7 node dots and 11 straight edges, plus J drawn as a Bezier curve fitted to the crop. Each edge has an arrow at its midpoint and the labels are in maths italic ($A,6$ etc.) at the crop's positions. I changed the crop's open chevron arrows to filled -latex heads (rule 4); most of the remaining red/blue in the overlay comes from that change and small label shifts. Rules 1, 3, 4, 11, 19.

Rectangle ABCD with arc PQ, drawn as a true circular arc about O through P and Q (angle POQ about 110 degrees as in the crop). PQ, OP and OQ are dashed in the house aux style and O is a dot. '2.1 m' is rotated along OQ as in the crop. NOT TO SCALE is kept and the layout follows the crop (rule 1). Rules 1, 3, 6a, 19.

Blank grid: x from 0 to 10, y from 160 to 240, with an axis break (zigzag) between 0 and 160. Major lines are every 1 degree and every 10 MW; minor dotted lines are every 0.2 and every 2, and the vertical minor lines continue down through the break band as in the crop. Grid lines are grey (black!65 major, light dotted minor) instead of the crop's black, per the rule that grid lines stay light grey. Axes have arrows and tick labels and axis titles are at the crop's positions. Rules 2, 3, 13, 4a.

Same grid as 300_q34_1 at this crop's offset, with dots at the computed points (0,236) and (5,184) (rule 16). Grid lines are grey (house grid rule). The remaining red/blue is the scan's slightly uneven grid spacing against the exact even grid. Rules 16, 2, 3.

Triangle ABC drawn to the crop's proportions. The 60 and 25 degree angle marks are circular arcs centred on A and B, running exactly from one side to the other. The '12 m' label sits beside AC. Rules 1, 14, 22. Checker 23 Nov fix: 25 degree arc now runs exactly from BC to BA (it overshot BC and stopped short of BA).

Solution triangle with arcs at A (60 degrees), B (25 degrees) and C (95 degrees), each centred on its vertex and running exactly between the two sides. x is on CB and 12 m on AC, at the crop's positions and clear of the lines. Rules 1, 14, 22, 11. Checker 23 Nov fix: 25 degree arc now runs exactly from BC to BA (it overshot BC and stopped short of BA).

Bell curve drawn as a smooth, symmetric formula curve (a narrow normal plus a small wide component). This matches the crop's peak, its fat tails and its height at z without copying the uneven scan line (rule 10). The area left of z is stippled with house shade dots and the vertical line at z meets the curve exactly (rule 12). The curve is 0.9pt because it runs along the axis (rule 9), and the axis has arrowheads at both ends. Status is approx because the tail shape was fitted by eye. The low redraw score is mostly stipple dots landing in different places, plus the slightly thinner left tail.

Straight line through (-1,0) and (0,1) with arrows at both ends, 0.9pt (rule 9). Axes 0.6pt with filled latex heads; labels x, y, O, -1, 1 placed as in the crop. Left out the stray option-letter dot. Rules 1,2,3,4,9,11.

Exponential growth curve drawn from y=a·e^{bx}, fitted to the crop's y-intercept and end points, 90 samples, smooth, 0.9pt. Left arrow sits just above the x-axis as in the crop. Option-letter remnant left out. Rules 1,3a,4,9,10.

Concave-down parabola drawn from the equation, fitted to the crop's vertex (y=1), roots and arrow ends, symmetric, 0.9pt. Labels -1, O, 1, 1, x, y as in the crop. Option letter 'C.' left out (options are lettered in the page). Rules 1,4,9,10,11.

Two-branch hyperbola drawn from one point-symmetric equation fitted to the crop's (1,1) point and branch ends, 0.9pt, arrows on all four ends. The (1,1) dot sits on the drawn curve with its label beside it (rule 16). Overlay is under 0.85 because the sketch's branches are not exactly symmetric (the lower branch dips steeper near the y-axis); the redraw keeps them symmetric (rule 10). Option letter 'D.' left out. Worth a quick look first.
Histogram with 10 bars, positively skewed, heights measured from the crop; axes with arrowheads; 'Frequency' rotated, 'Score' below. Same frame as the other options (rule 7). Rules 1,2,3,4.
Negatively skewed histogram (mirror of A) in the same frame as options A and C (rule 7). 'Score' sits a few px left of the crop's because the label position is kept the same across the option set.
Symmetric (peaked) histogram, 10 bars, in the same frame as options A and B (rule 7). 'Score' label in the shared option-set position, a few px left of the crop's.

Histogram of 10 adjacent bars (roughly uniform heights) with arrowed Frequency (rotated) and Score axes, positions measured from the crop. Lines 0.6pt black, filled latex heads, label font reduced to normalsize in round 2 to match the printed size. Rules 1,2,3,4,6.
Hexagon network: 6 vertex dots, 6 edges, vertices at crop positions. 0.6pt lines. Rules 1,2,3,7.
Hexagon plus its three long diagonals through the centre, same frame as other options. Rules 1,3,7.
Hexagon plus two verticals and four crossing chords, edges exactly as in the crop. Rules 1,3,7.
Complete graph K6 on the hexagon vertices (15 edges). Rules 1,3,7.
Scatter plot: arrowed x,y axes, 4 points increasing, positions measured from the crop; label size matched in round 2. Remaining colour is 1-2 px dot/label offset. Rules 1,2,3,4,7,19.
Scatter plot: same frame as option A, 4 points decreasing (two stacked at right) at crop positions. Rules 1,2,3,4,7,19.

Scatter plot with four points rising left to right. Axes have -latex heads, 0.6pt; dots and axis labels x, y placed where the crop has them. Remaining blue is only the dots being slightly larger than the print dots. Rules 1,2,3,4,19.
Scatter plot with five points falling left to right. Frame and style match option C (rule 7). Remaining blue is the slightly larger dots. Rules 1,2,3,4,7.

Right-angled triangle with sides 10 and 8, hypotenuse x, angle theta, a right-angle box and NOT TO SCALE. Geometry matches the crop exactly. The scores fall short of 0.85 only because the label glyphs sit a few pixels off (font shapes and the NOT TO SCALE line spacing); no line is misplaced. Rules 1,2,3,6a,11,19.

Weighted network A to H. Round 1 had the diagonals C-H and G-D missing F, so they were redrawn as C-F-H and G-F-D (rule 12). Dots are filled; weights are placed beside the edges as in the crop. Rules 1,3,6a,12,19.
Same network as 36_q18_1 with vertex K and edges AK=12 and CK=10 added. Geometry is the same as q18_1 shifted down, so the two figures are consistent. Rules 1,3,6a,12,19.

Solution figure: four alternative minimum spanning trees joined by OR. Each tree's vertices, edges and weights are placed as in the crop. Round 2 moved G in the fourth tree, the CF weights and the two middle ORs. Known small difference: the two middle OR labels sit about 35 px right of the crop's position (cosmetic; the round limit was reached). Rules 1,3,6a,12,19.

Rectangular paddock with an internal fence. Dashed dimension arrows for x and y use the house aux dash with -latex heads at both ends. Each dashed line is broken around its label, so there is no white box and the background stays transparent (rules 5c,6a). Rules 1,3,4,6a.

I drew A=450x-1.5x^2 from its equation (rule 10) at the crop's scale: 20 m = 62.8 px and 5000 m^2 = 62.9 px, 90 samples, smooth, 0.9pt (rule 9), over -17.6<=x<=317.6 as in the crop. Minor grid is 4 m by 1000 m^2, major grid 20 by 5000, both grey. The axes, tick labels, A (m^2) / x (metres) labels and the equation are at the crop's positions. The equation has a \halo so the grid stops around it (rule 5b). Changed from the crop: on the true curve the '300' label would touch the curve, so I moved it slightly left, and '280' slightly left with it, keeping both below the axis (rules 11 and 24). The two labels now sit close together ('280 300'). A human should check this first.

Open rectangular container (back face, left face and floor) drawn at the crop's corner positions. Dimension lines are fine dashes (aux) with filled latex heads and extension ticks (rules 3 and 4): 35 cm vertical, with the line broken for the label as in the crop; 20 cm parallel to the floor's depth edge; 40 cm along the bottom. All lines are 0.6pt.

Blank V-t grid, t from 0 to 55 and V from 0 to 1100. Major grid every 5 min and 100 L; fine dotted grey minor grid at 1 min and 20 L, five per major as in the paper. Axes have arrowheads, tick marks and the paper's labels: V (litres) and t (minutes). Round 2 wrongly made the minor grid ten per major; I made one extra render to go back to five, so this used 3 rounds instead of the allowed 2.

Same grid as 36_q24_1, at this crop's scale. Tank A is V=1000-20t from (0,1000) to (50,0). Tank B is V=30(t-15) from (15,0) to V=1100. Both lines are 0.9pt (rule 9). The dashed aux arrow drops from the computed intersection (29,420) to the t-axis (rules 12 and 16). 'Tank A' and '(b)' have curved leader arrows with filled heads. The redraw score is just under 0.85 only because of where the faint dotted minor grid falls. Like 36_q24_1, this needed one extra render to fix the minor grid density (3 rounds instead of 2).

Triangular prism on a cube, drawn at the printed diagram's vertices. It is a printed diagram, not a hand sketch, so I kept its slightly non-parallel back ridge (rule 1). It keeps both right-angle marks and the NOT TO SCALE note. All dimensions (5 cm, 5 cm, 11 cm, 8 cm three times) are fine dashed lines with filled heads and extension ticks; each line is broken where its label sits, as on the paper. The depth label 8 cm is rotated along its edge. Checker 23 Nov fix: top-right 5 cm moved off the roof edge, beside its arrow (top-left 5 cm moved the same way).

Activity network: 7 nodes (filled dots), straight arcs A, B, D, E, F, G, H, I, J and the semicircular arc C. Labels such as A(14) are at the crop's positions, with A(14) rotated along its arc. Changed from the crop: direction marks are filled latex heads at mid-arc instead of the paper's open chevrons (rule 4). The remaining overlay colour is mostly that arrowhead style and the dot size.

Solution network with the same layout and Start/Finish labels. Each activity's two-cell box is at the crop's position: A 0|12, B 0|2, C 0|0, D 8|8, E 20|20, G 20|35, F 26|26, H 36|36, J 36|39, I 44|44, and 46|46 at Finish. The D box has a curved leader arrow to its node. Direction marks are filled latex heads, not open chevrons (rule 4). All lines are 0.6pt.

Garden on an 8x5 grey grid, drawn in the crop's pixel units. The boundary is a Bezier dip from the top-left corner to (215,260) and back up to the dot at (336,102), then a symmetric parabola to the dot at (651,102). The region under the boundary is filled with the house stipple (shade dots, lightened to black!45), with the three dots (pt). The redraw-side score is low only because the stipple dots are placed differently (allowed under the procedure); the grid lines and curve match. Rules 1, 3, 5, 5a, 10.

Two trapezia with the curved garden edge, at the same scale and offset as the question figure. The crop's fine dotted top edges are drawn with the house aux dash. Labels 25 m / 20 m / 20 m / 20 m / 20 m are placed as in the crop and clear of the lines. Rules 1, 3, 6a, 11.

Directed flow network A–F with the same node positions and capacity-label positions as the crop. The crop's open chevrons halfway along each edge are replaced by filled -latex heads at the same positions (rule 4). Node dots and italic node labels. Rules 1, 4, 6a, 19.

Same network as q30_1, using the crop's positions. The cut is a curved dashed line (house aux) crossing BD, AB, BC and AC, matching the crop's arc. Filled mid-edge arrowheads replace the open chevrons. Rules 1, 3, 4, 6a.

North line with a filled arrowhead and bold N. P, A and B as dots, with segment labels 7 km and 9 km placed as in the crop. The angles are copied from the crop, which is a sketch, not redrawn to the true bearings 035/100 (rule 1). Rules 1, 4, 6a.
Regular decagon (circumradius 157 px, centre O) with side AB on top. OA and OB are dashed (aux), each with one equal-length tick at its midpoint. O is a dot with its label below. Rules 1, 3, 6a, 19.

Bacteria graph, y = 1000*2^(n/20), plotted smooth at 0.9pt. It runs from 1000 at n=0 to 8000 at n=60, through (20,2000) and (40,4000) as in the crop. Major grid lines (every 10 min / 1000) are solid dark grey and minor ones (every 5 / 500) fine dotted grey, so the grid is lighter than the crop's near-black. There are tick marks below the axis, a rotated y-axis title and filled axis arrowheads. The only differences left are grid-line greyness and weight. Rules 3, 3a, 4, 9.
Box plot (min 13, Q1 19, median 22, Q3 25, max 27) drawn at 0.9pt. Light grey vertical grid lines at every degree from 13 to 28, a 0.6pt axis with ticks, and the axis title centred. Rules 3, 9, 20.
Square with a tick mark on each side and the label '8 cm' below. Round 2 set the label to \normalsize so it matches the printed size. Rules 1, 2, 3.

Rectangle with single ticks on the long sides, double ticks on the short sides, and labels '3 cm' and '11 cm'. Scores are a little under 0.85 because the scan's strokes are thicker and the serif text sits slightly differently. Geometry matches. Rules 1, 2, 3, 6a.

Triangle drawn at the crop's pixel positions. Each side has a tick at its midpoint, set perpendicular to the side; '10 cm' is below the base. Round 1 failed because of a calc syntax mistake (the tick lines ran off the page); round 2 uses the computed tick ends. Rules 1, 3.
Isosceles trapezium labelled 3, 4 and 9 cm, with equal-side ticks on both legs. The ticks are mirrored about the centre line; the crop's right tick is a few px off. Rules 1, 3, 6a.

Network with vertices A to E. Edges are AB (one straight and one curved), BC, CD, DE, EA, AC and CE, with filled vertex dots and italic labels. Round 2 fixed the vertical scale, which round 1 had measured wrong. Rules 1, 3, 19.

Column graph of daily downloads for 20 days. Bars are grey (black!35, lighter than the scan's grey) with white dividers; the y axis runs 0 to 140 in steps of 20, both axes have arrows, and the axis titles are text. Labels use the house serif font instead of the crop's Helvetica. Rules 3, 4, 5, 6, 19. Checker 23 Nov fix: Day moved down, clear of the day numbers.

Option A (concave cumulative bars). Heights read from the crop; ticks every 100, labelled every 200. After 2 rounds some faults remain: the bar pitch is about 1 px too wide, so bar 20 runs about 25 px past the original. The day numbers sit about 10 px too low, and 'Day' nearly touches the '9 10' labels. Fix: pitch 31.7 px, day labels anchored at y 247, 'Day' at y 300. Rules 3, 4, 5, 6. Checker 23 Nov fix: Day moved down, clear of the day numbers.

Option B (convex cumulative bars). Heights read from the crop. Same faults as 38_q7_2: bar pitch slightly too wide (bar 20 overshoots), day labels a little low, and 'Day' close to the '9 10' labels. Same fix as 38_q7_2. Rules 3, 4, 5, 6. Checker 23 Nov fix: Day moved down, clear of the day numbers.

20-bar cumulative column graph drawn in the crop's pixel frame. Bar heights read from the crop (0.241 px per download). Bars are flat grey black!30 with 1.6 px transparent gaps (rule 5: the dark scan grey lightened). Axes have filled Latex heads (rule 4), ticks every 100 on the y-axis drawn once, lines 0.6pt. Text is in the house serif instead of the paper's sans (rule 19). The low original-ink score comes only from the solid grey fill differing in tone; all bar edges, labels and axes line up in the overlay. Uses the same frame as 38_q7_5 (rule 7).

Same frame and style as 38_q7_4 (rule 7). Bar heights read from the crop: 80 to 828, rising steeply from day 15. Fill is black!30. The low original score is only the grey fill tone; edges and labels match in the overlay.

Decreasing exponential, fitted as a smooth exponential through the crop's y-intercept (label 10) and end positions. It levels off slightly above the x-axis, as in the crop. Curve 0.9pt (rule 9), axes 0.6pt with filled arrows, italic x and y. Same frame and style as the other q10 options.

Decreasing exponential with y-intercept labelled 8, drawn smooth from an exponential fit. After two rounds the middle of the curve sits about 5 px below the crop's (it bends slightly sooner), which is why the redraw score is 0.75. The intercept, both ends and all labels match. Rules 9 and 10 applied.

Increasing exponential with the y-intercept labelled 10. It is a smooth exponential with a small offset, fitted to the crop's start, intercept and end; label clear of the curve. Curve 0.9pt, filled arrow heads.
Increasing exponential with the y-intercept labelled 8, a pure exponential fitted to the crop. Curve 0.9pt, filled arrow heads; same style as the other q10 options.

Two-level tree drawn with the house tree_style template (rule 21), branch run 2.05 cm to match the crop. 3/8 sits above the up-branch and 5/8 below the down-branch, as stacked \dfrac (rule 23) at the template's fixed probability size, which is a little smaller than the paper's. The second level is left unlabelled, as on the paper. P and C are kept upright as in the question text. The leftover overlay colour is only the smaller fractions and the 0.6pt line weight.

Smooth sketched boundary curve (no equation given) passing exactly through the marked dots (0,1.2), (6,2) and (12,1.4) (rule 16). The max near x=4.7 and min near x=10.5 are placed as in the crop. The region under the curve from x=0 to 12 is shaded with shade dots (rule 5). Double-headed height arrows have filled Latex heads (rule 4), broken around their labels; the label 2 inside the shading uses \halo (rule 5b). Ticks 1 to 12, O, x and y as in the crop.

Bearing diagram: N and E arrows, line AB at 25° below east, dot at B, labels A and B in maths italic, N and E upright as on the paper, NOT TO SCALE note. There is no angle arc because the crop has none. All arrows are filled Latex heads and all lines 0.6pt. The overlay score is below 0.85 only because the text glyphs and the scan's stroke thickness differ slightly. The geometry overlays the crop. Rules 1, 3, 4, 11, 19.

Hemispherical tank: an elliptical rim with a half-ellipse bowl at the crop's size. Centre dot, and two filled-arrow pieces either side of the '2 m' label going from the centre to the rim. Rules 1, 3, 4.

Weighted network with 8 towns at the crop's positions. The Kingsville–Underwood (65) and Walltown–Fernville (20) edges are smooth Bézier curves. All weights and town names are at the crop's positions. Round 2 moved Queentown's node and the 40/45 weights onto the crop's positions. Rules 1, 3, 11.
Blank axes: P vertical and t horizontal, with filled arrowheads and italic axis letters at the crop's positions. Rules 1, 3, 4, 19.

An 8×5 1-cm grid: light grey inner lines and a 0.6pt black border. The crop's border is heavier, but rule 3 limits lines to 0.6pt. The remaining blue in the overlay is anti-aliasing of the grey grid lines (a faint grid, which the spec accepts). Rules 3, 6.

Scatterplot with solid major grid lines at each integer x and every 4 on the y-axis, and dotted minor lines at y = 2, 6, …, 30. The grid is drawn grey, not the crop's black (grid lines stay light). Five data points. The dashed regression line is the computed least-squares line y = 3.2x + 2, which matches the crop. Axis titles and tick labels are as on the paper. Rules 1, 3, 6, 16.

Semicircle on the dashed diameter XZ, with Y on the arc. The two segments between the arc and the chords XY and YZ are filled with the house stipple. Right-angle mark at Y, the 30° label (no arc, as in the crop), centre dot at O, NOT TO SCALE note, and a 16 cm dimension line with filled arrows and end bars. Y is on the true circle, placed to match the crop (∠YXZ is drawn about 29°, which the NOT TO SCALE sketch allows). Rules 1, 5, 5a, 11, 22.

Scatterplot with 17 points read off the crop, a dotted grey grid, a frame, and the dashed regression line y = 29.2 − 0.011x drawn from the equation over the crop's span (x = 110 to 865). The title is centred over the plot area. The paper's title is bold sans-serif; the redraw uses bold house serif so there is only one font (rule 19). The right edge of the frame is about 8 px short of the crop's. Rules 1, 6, 19, 20.

Scatterplot redrawn in crop pixel units. Boxed plot area, dotted grid every 5, all 17 points placed from the crop, and the dashed regression line drawn from y = 45.6 - 0.683x over the crop's x-range (rule 16). Title is centred over the plot (rule 20). It is in bold house serif rather than the paper's sans, for one font (rule 19). Remaining colour is the faint dotted grid and slight thickness differences in the scan's text. Rules 1, 2, 3, 19, 20.

Blank graphing grid: x 0-35, y 0-40, square cells. Major lines every 5 are solid black at 0.6pt. Minor lines every 1 are light grey dotted (grid rule). Tick marks and labels every 5, plus x and y axis arrows with filled Latex heads (rule 4). Remaining red is the original's darker minor dotted grid.

Parabola fitted to the crop's roots (x=-10 and 100 marks), vertex and intercept dot. The sketch is not to scale, so these were not moved to the true R values (rule 1). The relevant part 0<=x<=100 is solid at 0.9pt (rule 9); x<0 and x>100 are aux dashed as in the paper, and the y-intercept dot sits on the curve (rule 16). The low redraw score comes from the 0.9pt curve against the scan's thin line and small differences in curvature.

Network diagram with node positions from the crop. Edge arrows are filled Latex heads at about the midpoint, replacing the paper's open chevrons (rule 4). Activity labels are in maths italic (rule 19); Start and Finish are text. Remaining colour is the chevron-to-Latex arrow change.
Triangle ABC with vertices placed as in the crop, which is NOT TO SCALE (rule 1). The 28°, 25 cm, 16 cm and NOT TO SCALE labels are as printed. There is no angle arc because the paper has none.

Standard normal curve drawn from the Gaussian formula, centred at the crop's 0 line, with the crop's peak height and spread (rule 10). The area between 0 and z is shaded with house stipple (rules 5 and 5a). The paper's curve is flatter-topped with tails that flatten sooner than a true Gaussian, so the tails differ by a few px. Most remaining colour is stipple-dot placement and the 0.9pt curve (rule 9) against the thin scan line. Status approx because the shape follows the true normal curve, not the drawn one.

Radial survey with O, A, B, C, D, all labels, bearings, dashed North arrow and NOT TO SCALE placed from the crop. Triangle OCB is house stipple (rule 5) and its 466 m^2 label uses \halo (rule 5b). The paper's heavy lines DO, DC and OC (triangle DOC) are drawn at 0.9pt rather than 0.6pt so the fenced triangle still stands out; owner may prefer 0.6pt. Low redraw score is only stipple density.

Blank normal curve over an axis with 7 evenly spaced ticks at the crop's positions. The curve is a true Gaussian at the crop's centre, height and approximate spread (rule 10), not the hand-traced shape, which is flat-topped with kinks near the shoulders. Overlay colour is that shape difference plus the 0.9pt curve (rule 9). Status approx because the true normal curve was chosen over the drawn one.

New sketch from the worked solution. A at the origin with a north arrow (N) and an east line (E). AB runs 25° below east to B. There is a 25° arc between E and AB, and a 115° arc with an arrow from A's north to AB. At B a dashed north line (N) and a 295° clockwise arc with an arrow run from north round to BA. The arc ends exactly on BA (rules 12, 22). The B label sits in the gap between the north line and BA so it does not touch the arc (rule 11). All lines 0.6pt, latex heads (rules 3, 4). No crop, so no overlay.

Minimum spanning tree drawn on the crop's own vertex positions, measured from the crop's pixels: Queentown, Kingsville, Underwood, Minertown, Walltown, Parktown, Citadel and Fernville. It has 7 edges: 30, 25, 20, 10, 15, 40 and the curved Walltown–Fernville edge of 20, total 160. Town names are upright text as on the paper, at 12pt Times, the same size as the crop. Lines are 0.6pt and vertices are filled dots (rules 1, 2, 3, 6a). The remaining colour in the overlay is a 1–3 px offset in the glyphs of the town names.

P = 2000(1.2)^t plotted from t = 0 to 5.6, smooth with 90 samples at 0.9pt (rules 3a, 9). Dots are at the computed points (0,2000) and (5,4977) (rule 16), with dashed guide lines to both axes (rule 12). Tick labels 5, 2000 and 4977, origin O. Axes run to t ≈ 6.4 and P ≈ 6400 (rule 13).

Light grey grid every 5 for x 0–35 and y 0–40, with axis arrows past the grid. Lines x+y=31 and 2x+y=38 drawn at 0.9pt between their intercepts (rule 9), each labelled with its equation clear of the lines (rule 11). Dot at the computed intersection (7,24), labelled (rule 16).

Option C: increasing, concave-up curve that leaves the y-axis horizontally at the lowest tick level and ends in a dot at t=2, top tick level. Same frame as the other options (rule 7). Curve at 0.9pt (rule 9).

Option D: decreasing, concave-down curve that leaves the y-axis horizontally at the top tick and ends in a dot at t=2, lowest tick level. Same frame as the other options (rule 7). Curve at 0.9pt (rule 9). The redraw score is lower only because the 0.9pt curve and the larger dot are heavier than the crop's hairline.

Pareto chart: seven bars (8000…500) with value labels, day labels, left revenue axis with ticks 1–10, right cumulative-percentage axis with ticks every 10% labelled 20–100, bold axis titles. Same Pareto chart as the question at the solution crop's scale. Drew y=-2/x-1 from its equation at the crop's scale (1 unit = 113 px across, 70 px up), both branches 0.9pt with arrows at both ends as in the crop. Overlay 0.29/0.41: the difference is the thick handwritten strokes and lettering. Rules 1, 3, 9, 10, 13, 16, 17.

Triangle ABC: C due north of A on the North axis, and AB at 49 degrees from north, as in the crop. North and East axes have filled latex arrowheads. Labels A, B, C, 12 km, 9 km and 50° sit where the crop has them (the crop has no angle arc, so I added none). In round 2 I re-measured the vertex positions. Overlay 0.79/0.76: the rest is the font and my 0.6pt lines against the scan's thin strokes. Rules 1, 3, 4, 6a.

Drew y=4x-e^x from its equation (x 66 px per unit, y 46 px per unit) and shaded the region from x=1 to x=2 in flat grey (the crop's grey), bounded by vertical lines. Axes have arrows at both ends; the curve is 0.9pt with arrow ends. The crop's freehand curve peaks further right (about x=1.6) than the true maximum (x=ln 4 ≈ 1.39) and its right arm is wider, so the curve sits a few px left of the crop's (rule 10: draw from the equation). Overlay 0.54/0.50, mostly because of that shift and the hairline scan curve. Rules 5, 9, 10, 27.

Drew y=4x^2-2x^3 from its equation at the crop's scale (1 unit = 374 px across, 91 px up) with evenly spaced ticks every 1/3. Tick labels: 2/3, 1, 4/3, 2 on x; 1, 2, 3 on y. Dots are at the computed points (0,0), (2/3,32/27), (4/3,64/27) and (2,0). I added coordinate labels to the inflection point and the maximum because the question asks for them; the crop marks those points with dots only. Changes from the crop: the y-axis is drawn level (it was tilted), the 2 label is moved below-left of its tick so it clears the curve, and I added x and y axis labels. Left out the teacher's working (factorisation, double/single zero notes, y-intercept working, red marking ticks) and the scribbled y-ticks (rule 17). Overlay 0.16/0.30, mostly from the working that was left out. Rules 1, 9, 10, 16, 17, 23.

Scatter plot on the crop's grid: x from 0 to 70, y from 0 to 60, a light-grey minor grid every 0.5 and a mid-grey major grid every 5 (the crop's grid is black graph paper). Blue axes are redrawn in black with arrows. The eight data points are plotted at their true values, and the line y=-0.77x+50 is drawn 0.9pt across the same range as the crop. The equation labels are placed as in the crop, using \halo on the grid. The vertical axis title is set as 'Temperature (°C)'; no horizontal axis title was added because it is cut off in the crop. Left out the teacher's extra ticks at the data values and the red marks (rule 17). Overlay 0.28/0.77: the crop's black grid is drawn here as a light grey grid (allowed), and the handwriting does not match. Rules 6, 9, 16, 17.

Drew y=sin x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π from its equation, 0.9pt, on a true scale (π/2 = 170 px), where the crop's ticks were uneven. The region between the curve and the x-axis from 0 to 3π/2 is hatched (shade hatch, as in the crop). Dashed lines run down from the maximum and up from the minimum, and the axes have no arrows, as in the crop. The 3π/2 label is moved above the axis, centred on its tick, because below the axis it would sit in the hatching and on the dashed line (21 Nov rule). The other labels are on the crop's sides. Left out the red marker comments. Overlay 0.24/0.38, mostly from the red comments and handwriting. Rules 5, 9, 10, 11, 17, 27.

Drew y=√(4x+8) (labelled y=2√(x+2) as in the crop) and the line 5y=2x+12 from their equations on linear axes (x 40 px per unit, y 55 px per unit). The region between them from x=-1 to x=14 is hatched. Dots are at the computed points (-2,0), (-1,2) and (14,8). The labels 2√2 and 2.4 are on the y-axis. The crop's x-scale is uneven: -2 and -1 are far apart and 14 is squeezed in. On a straight-line scale -2 and -1 sit much closer together, and the region is a long thin band (rules 12 and 16 take priority over the crop's proportions). Because of this the crop's tick label '2' is replaced by the label (-1,2) on the dot. Left out the ruled writing lines from the paper, the working and the red notes. LOOK FIRST: the tick labels -2 and -1 almost touch. The crop also has a lot of working text around the graph, which pulls the overlay's alignment off (0.04/0.15), so the overlay is not a useful check here. Rules 1, 9, 12, 16, 17, 27.

New sketch drawn from the worked solution: y=sin x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π, curve 0.9pt, axes with arrows, ticks at multiples of π/2. Intercepts are labelled O, π and 2π. Dots are at the maximum (π/2,1) and minimum (3π/2,-1), with dashed lines to the axis and fractions written as \dfrac. The region from 0 to 3π/2 is hatched to match 1318_q26_s1. The 3π/2 label is above the axis so it stays clear of the hatching. No overlay is possible because there is no original crop. Rules 5, 9, 10, 11, 16, 23, 27.

Circle centre (3,1), radius 3, drawn exactly at 0.9pt (rule 9: it touches the y-axis), with the centre dot, on a half-unit grid from x=-1..8, y=-3..6 (light grey; integer lines slightly darker). Axes have filled Latex heads at both ends, as in the crop (rule 4). x and y are in maths italic (rule 19). Tick labels are at the crop's size and positions with \halo over the grid. The low redraw score comes only from the grey grid, which the overlay does not count in the faint scanned original; the circle, axes and labels line up.

v-t curve has no equation, so it is a smooth spline fitted to the crop's turning points and intercepts (min near t=0.15, root about 0.7, max about 1.75, root about 3.3, min about 4.6, tail toward the axis), at 0.9pt. 9 evenly spaced ticks; labels 2,4,6 below the axis. The 8 label moved above the axis because the curve passes through its usual spot (21 Nov rule / rule 11). Filled arrowheads. The remaining red/blue is a curve offset of 1-3 px on the falling side.

Option A: smooth spline fitted to the crop (peak about t=1, root about 1.65, min about 2.5, root 5, small hump then tail), 0.9pt. The 2 and 4 tick labels moved to the mirror position above the axis because in the crop the curve runs through them (21 Nov rule, rule 11); 6 and 8 stay below. Same frame as the other options (rule 7).

Option B: smooth spline fitted to the crop (min about t=0.7, root about 1.45, max about 3.4, decaying tail), 0.9pt. Tick labels below the axis, as in the crop. Below 0.85 because of a 2-4 px drift along parts of the hand-fitted curve; the shape, turning points and roots match.

Option C: smooth spline fitted to the crop (min about t=0.7, root about 1.45, max about 3.4, shallow min about 8.2, then rising slightly), 0.9pt. Tick labels below the axis. Same frame and style as the other options.

Option D: smooth spline fitted to the crop (min about t=0.35, root about 0.7, max about 1.75, root about 3.8, then dropping steeply), 0.9pt. The 4 tick label moved above the axis because the curve crosses its usual spot below (21 Nov rule). CHECK: the moved 4 sits close to the curve where it crosses near t=3.8; it may need nudging right by a few px.

Triangle drawn on the crop's vertices with true circular angle arcs on both arms at the 23° and 130° vertices. Labels x, 8, 23° and 130° are at the crop's positions and size. Lines are 0.6pt. Rules 1, 2, 3, 11, 22.

Venn diagram from the solution, cleaned up: a straight rectangle and two smooth ellipses in black instead of the blue pen. The circled A and P are now plain maths-italic A and P. Values are 12, 10, 16 and 12 outside, which agree with the solution (22-10, 26-10, both = 10). The circles are slightly closer together so that 10 fits in the overlap without touching either circle. Low overlay scores come from the ruled paper lines, the hand wobble and the thick pen strokes in the scan. Rules 6, 10, 17, 19, 11.

Sector drawn on the crop's O, A, B. The arc is fitted through A and B with the crop's bulge (radius 270 px), because the figure is NOT TO SCALE. The segment is shaded with the house hatch reverse ('\\' direction). The house hatch is 45° and wider-spaced than the crop's steep fine hatching, and most of the remaining red/blue is this hatching difference. Labels and the NOT TO SCALE note are in place. Rules 1, 5, 5a, 11.

Axes, ticks (x = -1, 1, 2, 3, 4 on a true scale) and curve placed from the crop's pixels. The curve is one smooth spline through the crop's shape with zeros at -1, 0, 3, 4, drawn at 0.9pt. R1 and R2 are filled exactly between the curve and the axis, using black!30 instead of the crop's very dark grey (rule 5). Most of the remaining red is that lighter fill. Labels y=f(x), R1, R2, O, tick numbers and NOT TO SCALE are at the crop's positions. Rules 1, 3a, 5, 9, 13, 24.
Standard normal Z-table transcribed. Header 'first decimal place' spans the 10 value columns. The z cell spans both header rows. Rule 8.

notes: Plotted the true f(x)=x^3+3x^2-9x, smooth, at 0.9pt with arrows at both ends, on the crop's axes and origin. Marked points (-3,27), (-1,11), (0,0) and (1,-5) sit at their computed positions (rule 16). The scale is 60 px per unit in x and 7.5 px per unit in y, a compromise chosen because the sketch's own scale is inconsistent. As a result the maximum is about 30 px higher and the minimum shallower than in the sketch (rules 1 and 16 conflict here). The (-1,11) label moved to the lower left of its point, because upper right would touch the y-axis. Dropped: ruled paper, blue underlines and red ink (rules 6, 17). Low overlay is mainly the paper lines and the scan's thick margin line.

I drew f(x)=x^3-3x^2+4 from its equation at the crop's scale (101 px per unit) as a 0.9pt curve with arrows at both ends, over x in [-1.23, 3.1] to match the crop's curve ends. The 0.25-unit minor grid and 1-unit major grid are light grey. There is a tick every 0.25 on the x-axis, each drawn once and none at 0. Tick labels sit where the crop puts them, written with \halo so the grid shows through them. The f(x) label is the same size as the crop's. The open chevron arrows on the axes are now filled Latex heads (rule 4). The low redraw score comes only from my grid lines, which are darker than the faint grid in the scan; the curve, axes and labels line up. Rules used: 1, 2, 3, 4, 4a, 9, 10, 11, 13, 19, 24.

This is a hand-drawn solution sketch. I redrew both curves from their equations: f(x)=x^3-3x^2+4 and g(x)=-x^2+x+2, both 0.9pt with arrows at both ends. I kept the crop's layout and label positions. The intersections (-1,0), (1,2), (2,0) and the vertex (0.5, 2.25) are dots at their computed coordinates. The teacher's red crosses are gone. The vertex label keeps the crop's curved leader arrow; the leader crosses f, as it does in the crop. Labels 4, 2, -1 and 2 are kept, and so are the equation labels for f and g. The score is low because the teacher drew f far too flat on the right (it ends near y=3.4 at x=3.8). The true f is steeper and ends at (3.1, 4.96), so its right branch differs from the sketch. This was done on purpose (rules 10 and 16). Colour removed (rule 6). Rules used: 6, 9, 10, 16, 17, 3a, 4, 11, 13.

This is the 3D diagram with points M, O, A, B placed at the crop's pixel positions. It has all six edges, a right-angle mark at O, and true arcs for 20 deg at B and 22 deg at A. The h m height arrow is dashed (aux) with extension ticks. The 2000 m and 1000 m labels are rotated along their sides, and NOT TO SCALE is in bold. I drew the north arrow solid with a filled Latex head and left out the crop's faint dashed continuation. Rules used: 1, 3, 4, 6a, 11, 14.

I drew f(x)=x+1 and g(x)=(x-1)^2 from their equations as 0.9pt curves with end arrows, using the crop's scale. The shaded region runs from A along f to B, along g to C, then back along the x-axis. The crop's green fill is now house grey (rules 5, 6). Points A, B, C are dots at their true coordinates. Labels are in maths italic, including the x axis label, which is upright in the crop (rule 19). The axes have filled arrows at both ends. One difference: the left tail of f past A follows the true line, which is less steep than the crop's tail. Rules used: 1, 4, 5, 6, 9, 11, 12, 16, 19, 27.

I drew the two perpendicular roads with a right-angle box at R, the cross at the 100 km mark, and points B and A as dots. The distance r is a dashed line (house aux, which replaces the crop's dash-dot). The 60 km/h label is rotated, as in the crop, and both speed arrows have filled heads. Labels are at the crop's positions. Rules used: 1, 3, 4, 11.

This is a new plan-view sketch drawn from the worked solution. A is at the bottom and B is 1000 m due north of A. O lies on bearing 244 deg from B with OB=2220, so OA is about 2000 and O is almost due west of A. The sides are labelled 2000 m, 1000 m and 2220 m (the last along OB). The north line at B is labelled N. Angle ABO = 64 deg is a true arc between BA and BO. The bearing of 244 deg is a smaller arc going clockwise from north through east and south, with its arrowhead ending on BO. Everything is drawn to scale with room for the labels. Rules used: 1, 3, 4, 11, 14, 18, 22.

Scatterplot redrawn at the crop's pixel scale: light grey grid (every 10 mg, every 1 pain unit), axes with filled latex heads, minor ticks at odd y, 12 points at the crop's data values. Blue dots drawn black (rule 6). Round 2 reduced the label font to normalsize to match. Rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 19.

y = 0.5cos 2x plotted from the equation (smooth, 90 samples, 0.9pt) at the crop's scale and position, with arrowheads at both ends as on the crop. Zeros at ±π/4 and ±3π/4 are labelled with stacked \dfrac fractions below the axis, to the side of each crossing as on the crop. ±0.5 ticks on the y-axis. Round 1 failed to compile (pixel-unit plot overflow), so the curve was redone in a scaled scope. Rules 1, 3a, 4, 9, 10, 11, 23, 24.

Scatterplot of height against years: grey grid (1 year by 0.5 m), major and minor y ticks, 8 points at the crop positions (year 5 missing, as in the question). Blue dots drawn black. Fonts set to normalsize in round 2. Rules 1, 2, 4, 6, 19.

Pareto chart: grey bars (1100, 500, 100, 100, 75, 50, 50, 25; total 2000) and a cumulative % line (55, 80, 85, 90, 93.75, 96.25, 98.75, 100%) drawn black at 0.9pt instead of red (rule 6). The overlay scores are below 0.85 only because the crop's sans-serif and Excel fonts differ from the house font (rule 19), and because the crop includes a stray line of question text ('the graph to answer...'), which was left out on purpose.

Sketch curve traced from the crop as one smooth spline (0.9pt, rule 9) through (-3,0) and (5,0), with the shoulder near x=-1 and the minimum (2,-6) kept where the sketch puts it (not to scale, rule 1). The axes have double arrows, and the labels are in the same places as on the crop. Original-side coverage of 0.818 is due to the scan's heavier stroke and font differences. Rules 1, 3a, 4, 9, 11, 19.

Two horizontal box plots (Group 1: 52, 54.5, 64, 66.5, 70; Group 2: 53.5, 58, 60, 64, 69.5) above a double-arrow number line from 50 to 72, with integer ticks and labels and half-unit minor ticks. All five values of every box line up exactly (black in the overlay). The low overlay score comes from the number line and its labels sitting about 10 px lower than in the crop, and from the whisker end caps being a little shorter. I did not fix this because the 2-round limit was reached. Rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 9.

Blank sketching grid: x from -5 to 15, y from -6 to 11, one unit per square. Grid lines are light grey, with lines every 5 units slightly darker as on the paper. Axes have unit ticks, longer at multiples of 5, and labels -5, 5, 10, 15 / 10, 5, -5 on the same sides as the crop. The crop's open chevron arrowheads are replaced by filled Latex heads (rule 4). Axis letters are maths-italic x, y instead of bold (rule 19). Rules 2, 3, 4, 19, 24.

Same grid as 459_q11_1. Plotted y=sqrt(x+1) for -1<=x<=15 (smooth, sampled through u=sqrt(x+1) so the start at x=-1 has the right vertical tangent) and y=11-x for 0<=x<=15, both 0.9pt (rules 9, 10, 3a). The sketch's dots are kept at their computed positions (rule 16): (-1,0), (0,1), (0,11), (11,0), the intersection (8,3), and the end points (15,4) and (15,-4). The scan's grid is faint and broken; I drew the full light-grey grid, and that grid accounts for most of the blue in the overlay. Upright x, y are drawn as maths italic (rule 19); arrowheads are filled Latex (rule 4).

Blank d–t grid: 12 hour columns and 16 depth rows. Rows at 5, 10 and 15 and the vertical lines are mid grey; the other rows are light grey, as on the paper. The d-axis has ticks at every unit, longer at 5, 10, 15. The t-axis has a tick crossing it at every hour. The paper has no tick labels, so none are added. Filled Latex arrowheads (rule 4); maths-italic d, t (rule 19). Rules 2, 3, 4.

Same grid as 459_q12_1. The curve is d=4cos(pi t/6)+11 for 0<=t<=12, drawn from the equation at 0.9pt rather than traced from the uneven pen line (rules 10, 9). It has dots at (0,15), (3,11), (6,7), (9,11) and (12,15). The level d=13 is a fine house dashed line (aux, rule 3) and meets the curve at t=2 and t=10, matching the solution's 10 am and 6 pm (rule 18). The handwritten tick labels are replaced by clean typeset ones (rule 17): 1–15 on the d-axis and 8 am, 9, 10, 11, 12 pm, 1, …, 8 on the t-axis. The remaining red/blue in the overlay is the handwriting and the pen wobble of the original curve.

Upward parabola, vertex left of the y-axis, -1 label right of the y-intercept. Drawn as an exact parabola fitted to the crop's vertex and arm ends (rules 1, 10). Curve 0.9pt with filled arrowheads (rules 4, 9). Axes 0.6pt with arrows at both ends. Label uses the maths minus sign. Same frame as the other options (rule 7).

Upward parabola, vertex right of the y-axis, -1 label left of the y-axis. Exact parabola fitted to the crop (rules 1, 10). Curve 0.9pt with arrows at both ends (rule 9). Same frame as the other options (rule 7).

Downward parabola, vertex right of the y-axis, -1 label left of the y-axis and clear of the curve (rule 11). Exact parabola fitted to the crop. Curve 0.9pt with arrows at both ends. Same frame as the other options (rule 7).
Downward parabola, vertex left of the y-axis, -1 label right of the y-axis. Exact parabola fitted to the crop. Curve 0.9pt with arrows at both ends. Same frame as the other options (rule 7).

Curve starts at the origin with a vertical tangent, then decreases and is concave up. Drawn as a scaled -sqrt(x) curve fitted to the crop. Dot at x=1 sits on the curve (rule 16), with '1' above the axis as in the crop. Curve 0.9pt with an end arrow.

Clean redraw of the hand sketch of y=2x^2/(x^2-1). The curve is the real function at 106 px per x unit and 59 px per y unit, so the asymptotes x=±1 and y=2 and the inner branch match the sketch. Labels x=-1, x=1 and y=2 moved off the curve arrowheads (rule 11); y=2 now sits below its line. Dropped the ruled paper, 'even function' and 'd)' (rule 17). Asymptotes use the house fine dashes with arrows at both ends; curve 0.9pt. Low overlay is mostly the ruled lines and handwriting, plus the moved points and ink-box alignment.

Clean redraw of the hand sketch of y=-x^5+15x^3. The curve is the real function at 75 px per x unit and 2.16 px per y unit, sized to the sketch's turning points. The sketch is lopsided and much wider at the x-intercepts; the true curve is symmetric about the origin, so the minimum moves from x≈193 to 158 and the arms are narrower (rules 10, 16). Dots at (0,0), (3,162) and (-3,-162) are on the curve. Dashed lines at ±3/√2 meet the curve (rule 12). Tick labels keep the sketch's sides: 3/√2 below the axis, -3/√2 above (rule 24), written as stacked fractions (rule 23). Dropped the ruled paper and 'c)' (rule 17). Low overlay is the ruled lines, handwriting and the corrected curve shape.

Coastline on the x-axis with lights at (-8,0) and (8,0), origin O, dashed ship path y=b with P(x,b), and a double-headed arrow b broken around its label as in the crop. Arrows are filled Latex heads (rule 4). The dashed line uses the house fine dashes instead of the crop's long dashes (rule 3). Overlay just under 0.85 only because of the dash pattern and glyph and stroke differences.

Option A: y = 2 + 2/(x-1) on a -7..7 dotted light-grey grid. I drew it from the equation, which passes through the crop's (0,0), (2,4) and (7,2.33). I did not fix this because of the 2-round limit. Next fix: label inner sep 1pt, or move 4 and 5 to the right as well.

y = tan(2(x - pi/4)) drawn from the equation at the crop's scale: pi/4 = 79 px and 1 unit = 37 px. Overlay is 0.82/0.81; the remaining colour is label placement.

Drew y=sin(x-π/6) from its equation at the crop's scale: π/6 is 94 px, amplitude 170 px, x from -π/6-ish to past 4π/3. Axes have arrows at both ends; ticks every π/6; tick labels are stacked \dfrac. f(x)=2e^{-x/5} fitted to the crop: f(0) at the dot on the y-axis, and P at x≈4.52 placed on the curve where the crop shows it, not moved to the maximising x=5 (rules 1, 16). Standard normal probability table, transcribed (rule 8). Header row in bold; z values in the label column.

notes: Smooth symmetric normal curve from the formula, 0.9pt, at the sketch's size and position (rules 10, 9). 200/205/210 are fine dashed lines where the sketch places them (schematic, not true ±2.33σ; rule 1). The region from 200 to 210 uses house hatching, copying the sketch's diagonal strokes (rule 5). '98%' is moved inside the hatched region with \halo (rules 26, 5b). Scatterplot redrawn in pixel units. Axes are 0–80 mg by 0–10, with a light grey grid (vertical lines every 10, horizontal every 1), y ticks labelled at 2,4,…,10, short minor ticks at odd y, and arrowheads on both axes. The 12 points are plotted at their data coordinates. The blue dots are now black (rule 6) and lines are 0.6pt with filled latex arrows (rules 3, 4). What is left in the overlay is the change from the crop's sans-serif font to the house font in tick and axis labels, and the faint grey grid.
