Option B: upward parabola, vertex right of the y-axis, drawn from an exact quadratic fitted to the crop's vertex and end points. Curve is 0.9pt black; axes have filled latex arrows. Same frame and style as the other options (rule 7).

Option C: downward parabola, vertex right of the y-axis, drawn from an exact quadratic fitted to the crop's vertex and ends. It meets the x-axis where the crop does. Curve is 0.9pt black. Round 2 only fixed a LaTeX number overflow (squared term rewritten); the geometry did not change.

Option D: downward parabola, vertex left of the y-axis, drawn from an exact quadratic fitted to the crop's vertex and ends. It crosses the axes where the crop does. Curve is 0.9pt black. Round 2 only fixed a LaTeX number overflow; the geometry did not change.

Box plot over a plain time axis, with labels a, 12.1, 13.2, b, 18.1 and 'Time (s)'. Box, median and whiskers are 0.9pt (rule 9). The dotted drop lines down to the axis use the house aux dashes (rule 3). Round 2 moved the box top and bottom, the whisker height and the 'Time (s)' label to match the crop. What is left in the overlay is scan stroke thickness and small differences in the label glyphs.

y=x(x-4)(x-5) plotted from its equation at 0.9pt (rule 9/10). Both axes have arrows at both ends, x ticks every 1 and y ticks every 2, with labels at -12,-8,-4,4,8,12 as in the crop. Blue curve drawn in black (rule 6).

y=f(x) and y=-f(x), f=(x-2)(x^2+1), both plotted from the equation at 0.9pt and cut at |y|≈3.3 like the crop. The crop's blue and red curves are both black here (rule 6); the y=f(x) and y=-f(x) labels tell them apart. Stationary points (1/3,-50/27) and (1,-2) are placed at their computed positions (rule 16), with stacked fractions (rule 23). In round 2 the fraction label moved right of the y-axis so it no longer sits on the -1 tick label (rule 11). The scores fall short of 0.85 only because the labels are in a different font and the scan strokes are thicker; the geometry matches.

Cubic plotted from its equation. The region between the curve and the x-axis from x=0 to 4 is shaded black!30, not the crop's near-black fill (rule 5, 'too overkill'). The low original-side score is only that dark fill against the lighter grey; the lines, ticks and labels line up. Small GeoGebra-style tick labels, including both 0 labels, are kept as in the crop.

y=|1-x| on [0,2] with a light grey grid (lines every 0.5 in x and every 0.1 in y). The area for X≤1.5 has flat grey shade instead of the crop's blue fill (rules 5/6). The low original-side score is only the solid blue fill against grey; the lines match.

Same layout as q21_s1, with the area for 1≤X≤2 in flat grey shade instead of blue (rules 5/6). The low original-side score is only the blue fill (plus a page rule at the top of the crop, left out on purpose); the lines match.

3D sketch: ground triangle ABC in grey shade, PC solid and vertical, PA and PB in the house fine-dash style instead of the crop's long dashes (rule 3). Labels and lengths are \small to match the printed size. As in the crop, the angles carry values but no arcs. What is left of the colour is the crop's heavy long dashes and its different serif font. B sits 2 px lower than A, a tiny tilt to straighten if the owner wants (rule 1).

River cross-section: flat light-grey water band, grey section (flat shade, rule 5), surface line, six fine-dashed depth lines at equal 10 m spacing with right-angle marks, bold depth labels 3/22/29/30/28/5 m, 10 m dimension arrow, two (Ignore) labels with curved filled-arrow leaders. Bank traced as one smooth curve from the crop's positions (no scan wobble, rules 3a/10). Low original score is the scan's very heavy bank stroke and the wavy water texture, drawn at 0.6pt and flat grey (rules 3, 5). Labels in roman text, not sans-serif (rule 19).
Series circuit: two X boxes, terminal dots, wires. Box outlines 0.6pt, not the crop's heavy strokes (rule 3). That stroke weight is the only reason the original score is 0.75.

Parallel circuit: three X boxes plus a bottom box, a dash-dot continuation line between them, two vertical bus lines, terminal dots. The scan's dotted-looking bus lines are drawn solid (scan artifact). Positions matched in round 2.

Ladder: two slanted rails drawn as symmetric trapezoids. Top and bottom rungs solid double lines, five middle rungs as fine-dashed double lines (house aux). Dashed upward arrow, labels 7th rung / 1st rung. The crop's grey rungs are drawn black (rule 6).

x = 1 - cos 2t plotted from its equation over 0..pi with 90 smooth samples at 0.9pt (rules 3a, 9, 10). Axes have arrows at both ends as in the crop. Ticks at 1 and 2 with minor ticks at the halves; t ticks pi/4, pi/2, 3pi/4, pi written as dfrac (rule 23). Blue curve drawn black (rule 6).

Scatterplot on a 0-10 by 0-10 grid: light grey major lines, fainter minor lines at the halves, major and minor axis ticks, axis titles Years and Height (m). Eight points at (1,0.7),(2,1.4),(3,2.4),(4,3.5),(6,6.6),(7,7.9),(8,8.65),(9,9.5) as black dots (rule 6). What is left of the score gap is the faint grey grid and the crop's sans-serif digits vs the house serif.

Pareto chart: eight bars in grey with black outlines (rule 6; the crop has blue outlines with lavender fill), a cumulative % line at 0.9pt, left frequency axis 0-1200, right 0-100% axis with ticks, light gridlines, centred bold title (rule 20), category labels rotated as in the crop. The scan's tilt is straightened (rule 1). Bar heights are read from the crop (about 1110, 500, 100, 85, 55, 35, 25, 5), and the cumulative points are computed from these at the bar centres, so they are approximate. The crop's small red start dot is left out. Low scores come from the scan's thick blue outlines, the tilt and its slightly different label font.

Drew the normal curve from the formula (mean at the dashed line, 100 and 140 two standard deviations either side), fitted to the crop's size. Area between 100 and 140 shaded flat grey, as in the crop. Solid uprights at 100 and 140, a fine dashed line at the mean, a baseline, and bold labels at the crop's small size. The curve is 0.9pt because it runs along the baseline. Rules 1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 10, 26.

Drew two normal curves from the formula, with means, standard deviations and heights fitted to the crop (N1 narrow and tall to the left of O, N2 wide to the right). Labels N1, N2, x, y and O in bold italic as in the crop. Curves 0.9pt, axes 0.6pt with filled arrowheads. Rules 1, 4, 9, 10, 19.

There is no equation for this velocity curve, so I traced it from the crop as one smooth spline: it starts at the origin, dips, crosses the t-axis and flattens at the top right. P is a point on the drawn curve, labelled in maths italic (upright in the crop, changed for rule 19). The t-axis is extended to match the crop. It is 'approx' only because the curve shape comes from the trace. Please check that the spline looks smooth near P. Rules 1, 3a, 4, 9, 12, 19.

Redrew the matchstick patterns #1 to #3 cleanly: every square the same size, every roof and lower triangle the same shape, sticks drawn as 0.9pt strokes with small gaps at the joints. Stick counts match the question (6, 11 and 16), with shared sides as on the paper. The low overlay scores come from the scan's thick, uneven hand-placed sticks, which I regularised on purpose (rule 10). Please check the 0.9pt stick weight, which I used so the sticks read as objects. Rules 1, 3, 10.

Redrew the marker's sketch as a clean graph of the true curve y=3x^4-16x^3+24x^2-9. The y-scale is the crop's; the x-scale is stretched (not one to one) so the features are clear. The three points are plotted at their computed positions: (0,-9) min TP, (2/3,-67/27) POI and the flat (2,7) horizontal POI. Ticks 1, 2 and 7 are on a true scale. Removed the lined paper, the marking-scheme notes and the uneven hand ticks (rule 17). The overlay scores are very low because the sketch is not to scale: it put the POI at about x=1.2 and the x-intercepts in the wrong places. Labels are kept clear of the curve and the tick labels. Rules 9, 13, 16, 17, 23, 25.

Drew y=e^x(x+1) from the formula at the crop's scale (136 px per x-unit, 200 px per y-unit), with the minimum near x=-2, through (-1,0) and (0,1). Ticks at -2 and -1 below the axis and at 1 on the y-axis. The -2 label sits above the axis as in the crop, because the curve passes below there (rule 24). Labels O, x and y as in the crop. Curve 0.9pt. Rules 1, 4, 9, 11, 24.

Solution sketch redrawn cleanly. y=e^x(x+1) and the parabola y=1-1.5x-x^2 are both plotted from their equations at 0.9pt (rule 9). The parabola has arrowheads at both ends. Dots are at the computed points (0,1) and the maximum (-0.75,1.5625) (rule 16). The y-scale is about 155 px/unit so the true maximum fits; this puts (0,1) a little lower than in the sketch. I left out the teacher's marking notes and stray ticks (rule 17), which is the main reason the overlay score is low. The -2 label sits up and left of its tick because the parabola crosses the axis exactly at x=-2. The 1 label is between the two curves, clear of both (rule 11).

Normal curve fitted at the crop's size: mean at 4.5, sigma 0.595 on the crop's scale, drawn at 0.9pt. The teal tail beyond 5.5 is now flat grey shade (rules 5 and 6), with a vertical line at 5.5 and the label 0.0465 joined to the region by a filled-head arrow (rules 4 and 26). Round 2 reduced the font to match the crop.

Points A, P, Q, R and B are at the crop's positions. AP and BR are aux dashes, other lines 0.6pt, and points are small dots. Labels use maths italic in place of the crop's bold (rule 19); km stays upright text. The original score of 0.844 is just under target only because the crop's labels are bold and its lines thick.

Hand sketch on lined paper redrawn as a clean exam diagram (rules 10 and 17). It shows the true upper semicircle, centre (-2,1) and radius 5, on top of the rectangle from -7 to 3 of height 1. The axes are fitted to the crop's -7 and 3 marks. The overlay score is low because the hand-drawn semicircle is squashed and lopsided, and because of the ruled paper and handwriting.

y=sqrt(x) and y=x at the crop's scale, both 0.9pt and black (rules 6 and 9). P(1,1) is a dot at the computed intersection. x=k (k about 1.81, from the crop) is an aux dashed line. The region between the curves from 0 to k is flat grey shade, replacing the light blue fill (rule 5). Labels are maths italic, not bold (rule 19).

Standard normal density from its equation at the crop's scale (0.9pt, rules 9 and 10). Ticks and labels: -3 to 3 on the x-axis, 0.1 to 0.4 on the y-axis, f(x) and x as in the crop. Round 2 made the font smaller and lowered the axis tip. CHECK: the 0.3 label (and nearly 0.4) still touches the curve because the labels sit about 6 px too far left of the axis (rule 11). Fix by setting the label anchor to x=300 instead of 291; I did not redraw again because of the two-round limit. The original score is limited by label offsets only.

Sphere outline and dashed base ellipse are at the crop's size. Vertices A, B, C and D are at the crop's positions and lie on the ellipse. Hidden edges SB, AB and BC are aux dashes. T is placed at the true centre of the base, where the diagonals cross, about 10 px above the crop's T, with O directly above it on ST (rule 16). Labels are maths italic (rule 19).

Pareto chart drawn in pixel units. Bars 180/144/132/72/60/12 (total 600) are flat grey and the cumulative line goes through 30/54/76/88/98/100% at the bar centres. The line is 0.9pt (rule 9). The low score comes from the faint grid (the crop's minor grid is lighter and denser) and from the different font. Bars and line match closely.

Venn diagram: a frame with two equal circles. A and B are in maths italic (rule 19), replacing the crop's bold upright letters. Lines are 0.6pt, not the scan's heavy strokes (rule 3). The leftover colour is stroke thickness only.

Land profile above a lake. The shoreline is a smooth spline through the crop's positions and meets each dashed height line at its top (rule 12). Heights are not to scale, as in the crop (rule 1). The 40 m dimension arrows use filled latex heads (rule 4). The decorative ripple marks and bushes are approximate: ripples are small ~ glyphs and bushes are dense-stipple ellipses. One bush was moved left so it no longer sits under the second '60 m' label (rule 11). The low score is from these decorations.
Blank two-stage tree skeleton copied exactly: 6 straight branches, all with equal runs and a symmetric fan, at 0.6pt.

Completed solution tree drawn with the house tree template (rule 21): equal runs, symmetric fans, and stacked fractions (rule 23) above branches that go up and below branches that go down. W and L are in maths italic (rule 19). It also has the outcome column WW/WL/LW/LL, the P(..) column (1/1990, 39/1592, 39/1592, 3783/3980, checked against the solution), and First prize / Second prize headings centred on their columns. The low score is because the template's fonts and spacing are larger than the crop's tiny print. The layout matches.

Scatterplot on a 1-10 by 1-10 grid. Major grid lines are light grey and the half-unit horizontal lines are lighter still. There are half-unit minor ticks on the y-axis. The 8 points are read from the crop, with no point at year 5, and drawn black instead of blue (rule 6). Axes end in filled arrowheads.

Both curves are plotted from their equations, f=2sin x and g=(1/2)sin 2x, at the crop's scale. The region between them is filled flat grey (rule 5: light tone, not the dark scan grey) and the curves are 0.9pt (rule 9). Axes have double-ended arrows and y ticks every 1/2. The 3π/2 label sits on the shading with a halo (rule 5b). π is in the house maths font rather than the crop's upright π.

Axes with y=2sin x drawn from the equation at the crop's scale (π = 384 px, 1 unit = 187 px). The curve is 0.9pt because it touches the axis (rule 9). Arrows are filled Latex heads on both ends of both axes (rule 4). I moved the π label just left of its tick and the 2π label just right of its tick, both on the line below the axis, because the curve runs through the spots where the crop put them (rules 11, 24, 21 Nov). Rules 1, 3, 10, 13 also applied.

Both curves are plotted from their equations at the crop's 1:1 scale: h(x)=(1/3)sin 3x solid at 0.9pt, f(x)=2sin x in the house aux dash. Ticks every π/6 on x and every 1/3 on y. All x tick labels are stacked fractions (rule 23) on one row below the axis, set a little lower than the crop so they clear the dips of h (21 Nov rule). The 3π/2 label from the crop is kept. TO CHECK: in the final render the dashed f(x) looks to pass very close to, or touch, the 7π/6 and 11π/6 labels. I had no rounds left to nudge them; the fix is to move those two labels right. The overlay is low mainly because the label font and positions differ from the crop.

y=x^3+6x^2+9x is plotted from the equation on the crop's light grey grid. The curve is 0.9pt with arrow ends as in the crop. The four marked points are at their computed coordinates: (-3,0), (-2,-2), (-1,-4), (0,0) (rule 16). The four callout boxes are flat grey (house shade) with leader lines ending at the points. Box text is set in footnotesize so it fits inside the boxes. The x tick label -2 sat on the curve, so it moves above the axis; the y tick label -3 sat on the curve, so it moves to the right of the axis (rule 11, 21 Nov). Coordinates are typeset as maths, e.g. (-3, 0).

The v(t) sketch is fitted with smooth Bezier pieces through the crop's key points: flat to the t1 dot, maximum at t2, the t3 dot on the axis, and on to the end. The dashed guides at t2 and t4 end exactly on the curve (rule 12). The curve is 0.9pt. The crop's open chevron arrows become filled Latex heads (rule 4). The remaining red is mostly the scan's heavier strokes and dashes.

Blank x(t) axes with the faint grey dashed guide curve. The guide is the q28_1 velocity shape scaled 1.344x, as in the crop, with grey dots at t1 and t3 and a grey dashed line at t2. The guide uses the house fine dash at 0.9pt in black!35 (shade of grey, not colour; rules 3 and 6). The redraw overlay score is low only because the fine grey dashes don't line up dash-for-dash with the crop's long, thick grey dashes; the shape and positions match.

Smooth displacement-time sketch: flat at the starting height up to t1, inflection at t2, maximum at t3, decreasing through t4 and crossing the t-axis. The dashed guides at t1 to t4 end exactly on the curve (rule 12). I left out the stray small tick on the curve below the axis, which looks like a teacher's working mark (rule 17), and smoothed the kink near the end of the flat section (rule 10). Labels are a little larger than the scan.

River diagram drawn at the crop's positions: dashed riverbanks in the house aux dash, flagpole OF at 0.9pt for emphasis, lines OA, OB, FA, FB, a w m dimension arrow split around its label, and the S-shaped leader from the 60° label to angle AOB. The crop's superscript 0 becomes a real degree sign. I moved the 60° and 30° wedge labels slightly to clear the lines (rule 11). TO CHECK: the 60° label near A sits in a very narrow wedge, and its degree sign may be touching line OB.

Circle drawn through A, B and C, with the centre O computed from them (rule 16). Also drawn: the isosceles triangle, dashed OP labelled x, the right-angle mark at P, double tick marks on AB and BC, and the 'Not to Scale' note. Labels use maths italic, where the crop has bold italic (rule 19).

Stem-and-leaf plot, so it goes in as a table per the 12 Nov ruling (table.slp: no grid, one rule between stem and leaves). Each leaf is its own cell. The unknown leaf x is kept in maths italic. Rows 4 and 6 are padded with empty cells.

Cumulative frequency histogram drawn on a true scale (bars 52.5–87.5 km/h, heights 10, 40, 80, 130, 220, 280, 300), with a light grey grid every 2.5 km/h and every 50. 2019 box plot (10, 16, 23, 30, 36) at 0.9pt over the Marks axis from 4 to 40 with ticks every 2, plus the empty 2020 row, at the crop's size. The tick numbers are upright house maths font, not the scan's italic Times (rule 19); that font difference is the only thing keeping the scores below 0.85. Rules 1, 3, 9, 19.

2019 and 2020 box plots (2020: 10, 19, 30, 34, 38) at 0.9pt, both in black, with fine grey dashed guide lines to the axis as in the crop. The ordered 2020 data is set cleanly below with Q1 and Q3 arrows between the right values and Q2 circled at 30. Same scatterplot as 629_q15_1 at this crop's scale. The best-fit line is 0.9pt in black, from Maths 13 to Maths 97.6. The reading lines at Maths 90 meet the line exactly at English ≈59.1, which matches the solution's 59 (rule 12). The blue and green pen is now black (rule 6). Rules 1, 3, 6, 9, 12.
